characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: optical microscope; specimen electrolytically polished and etched with a solution of 1 g ferric chloride, 10 ml hydrochloric acid and 10 ml deionized water
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fig. 3 optical micrographs; the as-quenched state (before rolling) is not detailed in OM but the initial grain structure is equiaxed.
characterization_methods.purpose: investigate the initial microstructure and cold-rolled microstructure evolution

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TESCAN MIRA 3 scanning electron microscope; electrolyte for electrolytical polishing = deionized 10% water, 10% perchloric acid, 10% ethylene glycol butyl ether and 70% alcohol
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fig. 2(a,b): inverse pole figure map and phase map of the initial state; austenite colored blue, black lines = high angle grain boundaries (≥15°) and red lines = twin boundaries; almost random texture.
characterization_methods.purpose: characterize the initial microstructure, grain boundaries and texture

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2100 transmission electron microscope; twin jet electro-polishing with 30% nitric acid and 70% methyl alcohol
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fig. 2(c): nano-sized κ'-carbides appear as bright particles uniformly distributed in the dark austenitic matrix.
characterization_methods.purpose: observe nano-sized κ'-carbides in the austenitic matrix
characterization_methods.technique: transmission electron microscopy (TEM) dark-field imaging and selected-area diffraction

characterization_methods.key_findings: Initial texture before cold rolling was almost random distribution (reflected by the inverse pole figure).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: incomplete pole figures {111}, {200} and {220} measured on the RD × TD plane; ODFs and F_max calculated by the Arbitrarily Defined Cells method

characterization_methods.key_findings: As-quenched state: YS ~570 MPa, UTS ~830 MPa, UE exceeding 75%, indicating excellent work hardening capability.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1, dog-bone specimen gauge length 16 mm, width 4 mm, cut along RD, three parallel tests
characterization_methods.purpose: evaluate the mechanical properties of the as-quenched and cold-rolled states

analytical_models.equation_role: τ_c = 2 γ_SF / b_p (Eq. 1), relating the critical shear stress to the stacking fault energy and the partial-dislocation Burgers vector
analytical_models.model_name: critical shear stress for deformation twinning
analytical_models.model_note: SFE and b_p of the current steel estimated as ~108 mJ/m² and 0.146 nm; critical stress computed as ~1.48 GPa.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The calculated critical shear stress (~1.48 GPa) is much higher than the maximum resolved shear stress (~0.75 GPa), yet twinning was observed; attributed to SRO interaction lowering the actual critical shear stress and to local stress concentration from inhomogeneous strain.

analytical_models.equation_role: σ_TL = K · M · G · b / D (Eq. 2), expressing the strengthening by the long-range interaction between coplanar slip bands in the Taylor lattice
analytical_models.model_note: Strengthening by Taylor lattice attributed to long-range interaction between coplanar slip bands; later microbands, twins, shear bands and dislocation tangles strengthen via Hall-Petch effects.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: High Mn-Al-C austenitic low-density steel with nominal composition Fe-30Mn-11Al-1.2C (wt%) was fabricated by vacuum induction melting.
The cast was soaked at 1250 °C for 12 h to homogenize and refine the microstructure (upstream bar-fabrication step).
Then hot-forged into bars 60 mm in diameter with the finish forging temperature of 900 °C (upstream bar-fabrication step).
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: forged into bars 60 mm in diameter

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sheets 40 mm in width, 70 mm in length and different thickness (1.3, 1.7, 2.4, 4 and 6 mm) were cut from the bars using wire electric discharge machine.

The sheets were solution treated at 1100 °C for 1 h before any cold rolling; this gives the initial as-quenched austenitic state (0% rolling reduction). The as-quenched κ'-carbides form via spinodal decomposition during quenching.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile test using a SHIMADZU AG-X50KN universal testing machine; three parallel tensile tests per condition.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog-bone-shaped tensile specimen, gauge length 16 mm, width 4 mm, cut along the rolling direction

defects.type: annealing twins (twin boundaries present in large amount)

grain_structure.texture: almost random distribution (no preferred orientation) reflected by the inverse pole figure

phases_present.morphology: matrix (equiaxed grains, colored blue in EBSD phase map)
nano-sized particles uniformly distributed in the austenitic matrix; formed via spinodal decomposition during quenching

precipitates.distribution: uniformly distributed in the austenitic matrix

structures.overall_structure: As-quenched initial microstructure (before cold rolling) consisting of an austenitic matrix with nano-sized κ'-carbides uniformly distributed in it, containing a large amount of annealing twins; the phase constituent was estimated as austenite and κ'-carbides.

unmapped_findings: The stacking fault energy (SFE) of the present steel was estimated as ~108 mJ/m² and the Burgers vector of a partial dislocation as 0.146 nm (block b0007, b0045).
The maximum resolved shear stress reported for the steel was ~0.75 GPa (block b0045).
The as-quenched state shows a low yield strength and UTS of ~570 MPa and ~830 MPa, but a dramatic uniform elongation exceeding 75%, indicating excellent work hardening capability (block b0020).

With cold rolling the yield strength eventually reached ~2.0 GPa (approximately 3.5 times the as-quenched state); the as-quenched baseline (~570 MPa) is thus about 1/3.5 of the 90% rolled strength (block b0020).

The microstructure of the as-quenched material changes with cold rolling approximately in the sequence Taylor lattice, microbands, nano-twins, shear bands and dislocation cells (block b0007, b0047, b0066).
